newsitem.title: USA: Calif. sues BankAmerica over bond funds.
newsitem.headline: Calif. sues BankAmerica over bond funds.

text.p: California's attorney general on Monday sued BankAmerica Corp., the nation's third largest bank, for allegedly mismanaging billions of dollars of state municipal bond funds.
As a result of the bank's alleged actions, the attorney general said state and local governments suffered "hundreds of millions of dollars" in damages.

The lawsuit, filed by Attorney General Dan Lungren in San Francisco Superior Court, alleged that more than $100 billion of bond funds were placed in state and local government accounts administered by the bank between 1978 and 1993.
"The bank lost money in those accounts through errors, mistakes, theft and poor management," the lawsuit alleged.

The lawsuit was based on a so-called "whistleblower" complaint filed under seal in April 1995 by Patrick Stull, a former vice president for corporate trust at Bank of America. Lungren said his office investigated Stull's allegations for two years.
Lungren's suit was similar to one filed last week by San Francisco, which alleged BankAmerica mishandled hundreds of millions of dollars of bond funds and engaged in a massive cover-up.
Lungren's lawsuit names as defendants BankAmerica and its unit, Bank of America.
